findings.title: Use the correct process type when killing unhealthy workers
findings.body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances. These are not instances of multiprocessing.Process, so this check is false for production workers and process.kill() is never called. A worker declared hung therefore remains alive while its replacement starts flushing the same shards, potentially producing duplicates and updating the replacement's shared health/backpressure state. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess instead; the termination check in join() has the same problem.

findings.title: Terminate remaining workers when the join deadline expires
findings.body: When the shared deadline expires, this break skips cleanup for the current worker and every subsequent worker. For example, if the first worker consumes the timeout waiting for Kafka, none of the other workers receive termination, even after the process-type check is corrected. Setting stopped only stops workers once their current flush/produce call returns, so blocked workers can survive a rebalance after their strategy is discarded. Stop waiting when the deadline expires, but still terminate and reap every remaining process.
